questions.prompt: What are GitHub Issues primarily used for?

options.text: Tracking bugs, tasks, feature requests, and questions

questions.explanation: Issues track units of work and discussion — bugs, tasks, feature requests, questions — with labels, assignees, and milestones attached.

questions.prompt: Which will automatically close issue #12 when the pull request merges?
questions.explanation: A closing keyword (Fixes/Closes/Resolves) plus the issue number auto-closes the issue on merge. A bare mention like 'see #12' only creates a link.

questions.prompt: Which statements are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: Labels categorize issues and pull requests
Milestones group issues toward a goal or release
Projects provide boards and tables to organize work
Only the repository owner can ever open an issue

questions.explanation: Labels categorize, milestones group toward goals, and Projects organize work visually. Anyone with access (and the public, on open repos) can open issues.

questions.prompt: Writing '______ #12' in a pull request will auto-close issue 12 when it merges. (give one recognized keyword)
questions.explanation: Recognized closing keywords include Fixes, Closes, and Resolves (and their variants). Any of them followed by the issue number auto-closes it on merge.

questions.prompt: You merged a PR that fixes a bug, but the linked issue stayed open. What's the most likely reason?

options.text: The PR didn't use a closing keyword to link the issue
Issues can only be closed manually

questions.explanation: Auto-close requires a recognized closing keyword (e.g. Fixes #N). Without one, the issue isn't closed automatically even though the fix merged.

questions.prompt: Match each item to what it is.

pairs.right: A tracked task, bug, or request
A group of items toward a release

questions.explanation: Issues are the items, labels categorize them, milestones group them toward a goal, and Projects visualize the workflow.
